messages.author: c3ac76bc87868f68
messages.subject: mardiaSkew (semTools)
parts:
Dear all,

we recently used the mardiaSkew-function in the semTools-Package to check for multivariate skew of our data set. During this we discovered that the p-Value that is returned is R's standard one-sided p-Value (determined via the pchisq()-Function in line 16 of the function). This results in the function returning large p-Values when the Null (no skew) is violated. I wanted to check whether anyone can tell me if this is intentional, or whether it is simply a small typo in the function (and the intended result is provided by 1-pchisq()).

Thanks in advance! 

Best, Martin

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: mardiaSkew (semTools)
parts:
I think you're right, good catch. I just made the change on github, so it should go through when the next version of semTools is released.

Terry
